quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the side of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull to the right edge of the road and stop. Stay parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, move to the edge closest to you.

questions.question: Stopping distances and crash severity:
questions.explanation: Stopping distances are longer and crashes are more severe when you drive faster.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection at the speed limit when the light turns yellow. You should:

options.text: Slow down and go through without caution.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Stop at a yellow light if you can do so safely. Otherwise, cross the intersection with caution.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. You must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and doesn't use all of it.
Honk to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder so you can pass.
Move fully into the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move fully into the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give a motorcycle a full lane when passing. Never share the same lane. If you return to your lane too soon, the rider may have to swerve into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when rain first starts. When the road is slippery, you should:

options.text: Test your tires on an uphill road.
Look less far ahead of your vehicle.

questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire traction. Drive slower on wet roads than on dry roads. Avoid fast turns or stops to reduce the risk of skidding.

questions.question: The proper way to make a right turn is to:

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the center line before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach in the right lane, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, use your signal to warn other drivers. Slow down and stay as close as possible to the right curb as you approach the intersection.

questions.question: When stopped at a red light with a green arrow, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow if you:

options.text: Come to a complete stop first.
Are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can proceed in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane and no pedestrians or vehicles are in the intersection. Yield to anyone already in the intersection.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle:

options.text: Expect the child to have full control of the bicycle.

questions.explanation: Young bicyclists can be unpredictable and may change direction suddenly. Children and bicycles are small and hard to see, so stay alert.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Use high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Use high beams only on rural roads when no other cars are nearby. Switch to low beams when following another driver closely.

questions.question: Before entering a curve:
questions.explanation: You may drive slower than the posted speed limit based on conditions, but never faster. Reduce speed when approaching curves, hills with limited visibility, slippery roads, or areas with animals and pedestrians.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you must:
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should be alert and careful. Slow down when you see this light.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Trucks are not allowed on this hill.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers about a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed to protect your brakes.

questions.question: Alcohol is:
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down your thinking and body functions. It reduces inhibitions and hurts your ability to focus and stay alert.

questions.question: A bad suspension can cause:
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and gives you a smooth ride. If your car bounces a lot over bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass another car:

options.text: If the car ahead is turning left.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver won't expect you there and may drive off the road.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should:

options.text: Watch for traffic coming from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for traffic coming from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to dangers ahead. They are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you about traffic merging into your lane from the right.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Locks your front wheels, so you can't steer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks your front wheels, so you can't steer.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock your front wheels and cause you to lose steering control. Drive slowly in bad weather to avoid hard braking.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug, whether it is illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. You can turn left onto another one-way street only if:

options.text: You speed up before the turn.

questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the left, if there is no sign stopping you. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a stop sign is ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and look both ways before going.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for traffic, and go with caution.

questions.question: When do you need to turn on your headlights while driving?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect light back at you, creating glare and making it harder to see.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast your body absorbs alcohol?
questions.explanation: Body weight, gender, food in your stomach, and number of drinks affect alcohol absorption. Only time removes alcohol from your system.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street to another one-way street, which lane should you start from?
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the far left lane of a one-way street.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: Get ready to let oncoming cars go.
Your protected left turn is ending.

questions.explanation: A yellow left turn arrow means your protected turn is ending and you must be ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
